newsitem.title: UKRAINE: UKRAINE REMITS AVTOZAZ DEBTS, AIDS GM/DAEWOO.
newsitem.headline: UKRAINE REMITS AVTOZAZ DEBTS, AIDS GM/DAEWOO.

text.p: Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma forgave carmaker AvtoZAZ's debts on Tuesday, lifting a barrier to plans by South Korea's Daewoo Group and U.S. carmaker General Motors to produce cars at AvtoZAZ.
A presidential spokesman said Kuchma, confirming a move last month by parliament, had signed a decree remitting the plant's debts, put by management at 98 million hryvnias ($52 million).

Besides the debt cancellation, the foreign companies want a law guaranteeing tax breaks for a joint venture they have formed at AvtoZAZ, which would upgrade the plant in the eastern city of Zaporizhya to build small- and medium-size cars.
The venture aims to produce a modernised version of Ukraine's Tavria and Dana cars, along with 150,000 units of Daewoo's three models and 45,000-75,000 Opels a year.

Daewoo won a tender and then formed a joint venture with General Motors, which was its main competitor. AvtoZAZ has a 50 percent stake in the venture with the rest going to Daewoo and GM, whose shares have not yet been announced.
Daewoo has said it is ready to invest up to $1 billion in the project.
